newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam to seek foreign aid for huge power plant.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam to seek foreign aid for huge power plant.

text.p: Vietnam plans to seek foreign aid for a hydro-electric plant in the remote northern province of Son La which would double the country's power capacity, an official at state-owned Electricity of Vietnam (EVN) said on Wendesday.

He said a pre-feasibility study for the 3,600 MW plant, estimated to cost US$3.5 billion to $4.0 billion, had been completed and the government was expected to give the go-ahead for a full feasibility study soon.
"EVN plans to mobilise capital from official development assistance as much as possible," he said. "The rest will come from domestic resources."
The EVN official gave no date for completion of the plant, though previous reports have said 2007 was the target.
Vietnam is planning to spend $1.0 billion to $1.5 billion per year to build 15 new power stations by 2010 to meet burgeoning demand.
The country currently has 12 power stations generating about 17 billion kwh a year, but demand is expected to rise by at least 11.6 percent a year between now and 2010.
